title: Proof by Contrapositive
short: To prove P → Q, prove ¬Q → ¬P instead: to show "if n² is even, then n is even," show that odd n gives odd n².
trouble: Students prove the converse Q → P by mistake, which is a different statement.

blocks.html: Sometimes a direct proof gets stuck because the hypothesis gives you nothing to compute with. Knowing that "$n^{2}$ is even" does not hand you a formula for $n$. The fix uses an equivalence you already know: a conditional and its contrapositive are true together.
To prove $P o Q$ by contrapositive, prove $ eg Q o eg P$ directly instead: assume $Q$ is false and show $P$ is false. Since $P o Q \equiv eg Q o eg P$, this proves the original statement.

The two statements have identical truth tables: each is false only when $P$ is true and $Q$ is false. So a proof of one is a proof of the other. The switch helps when $\neg Q$ is the easier starting point. "$n$ is not even" gives $n = 2k + 1$, something you can square and expand.

blocks.title: If $n^{2}$ is even, then $n$ is even
blocks.q: Prove: for every integer $n$, if $n^{2}$ is even, then $n$ is even.
steps: Contrapositive: if $n$ is not even (odd), then $n^{2}$ is not even (odd).
That is odd, so the contrapositive is proved, and with it the original statement.
blocks.a: Proved via: $n$ odd implies $n^{2} = 2(2k^{2} + 2k) + 1$ is odd.

blocks.title: An "or" in the conclusion
blocks.q: Prove: for real numbers $x$ and $y$, if $x + y \ge 10$, then $x \ge 5$ or $y \ge 5$.
steps: Negate the conclusion with De Morgan: not ($x \ge 5$ or $y \ge 5$) is $x < 5$ and $y < 5$.
Adding the inequalities gives $x + y < 5 + 5 = 10$. Done.

blocks.title: A linear expression
blocks.q: Prove: if $3n + 5$ is odd, then $n$ is even.
steps: Contrapositive: if $n$ is odd, then $3n + 5$ is even.
That is even, which proves the contrapositive.

blocks.html: Proving the converse by accident. To prove "if $n^{2}$ is even, then $n$ is even," some students assume $n$ is even and show $n^{2}$ is even. That proves the converse $Q \to P$, a different statement (and here an easier, true one, which makes the slip hard to notice). Check: the contrapositive starts from the negation of the conclusion and ends at the negation of the hypothesis. Both parts get negated, and they swap places.
